co_matron_the.blurb: The Matron is a tall spire on the ridge above Shadow Canyon, in the southern Flatirons outside Boulder. Most of its twenty-odd lines are trad, with a few bolted sport routes, and difficulty climbs from easy fifth class through a solid block of 5.9 and 5.10 to several 5.12 and 5.13 lines. The faces behave very differently: the north side stays cool and shaded, while the east ridge and south face catch the sun, and the west and southwest sides offer lower-angle options. It is visited less than many Flatirons formations, so it suits trad climbers who want multi-pitch variety and some quiet. Bolted anchors on top allow a rappel descent, and getting in is a proper hike.

co_overhang_rock.blurb: Overhang Rock is a big fin of rock in the southern Flatirons above Bear Canyon, near Boulder. Nearly all the climbing is on the yellow west side, which looms impressively from the canyon but looks unremarkable from the east. The route list splits into a handful of moderate trad lines in the 5.5 to 5.8 range and a dozen hard bolted lines, mostly 5.12 and 5.13, with almost nothing in between. That makes it more of a destination for strong sport climbers than for beginners, though the moderate trad lines are a fine warm-up. The trail in has been improved and is no longer a loose scramble, and the crowds are lighter than at many Flatirons crags.

co_der_zerkle.blurb: Der Zerkle is a small Flatiron in the central Boulder Flatirons, set among trees beneath Mallory Cave. Its faces range from slabby to overhanging, and the pocketed, hueco-like rock gives it more variety than its size suggests. Routes run one to three pitches, a mix of trad and bolted sport lines, plus an easy scramble up the west face. Most grades fall between 5.7 and 5.9, with a notable group of 5.11s and a single 5.12. Expect a blend of sun and shade, a steady uphill hike from the trailhead, and fewer people than at the headline Flatirons formations.

co_zoids_the.blurb: The Zoids is a spread-out stretch of the East Rim in Castlewood Canyon State Park, on the plains southeast of Denver. Climbing here is mostly trad and top rope, with a couple of bolted lines and two V2 boulder problems. Routes start around 5.7 and run through the 5.10s, with a few reaching 5.12. The canyon's conglomerate and sandstone can be sandy or crumbly in the cracks, so protection takes some care, and top-rope anchors may call for long slings or an extra rope. The cliffs are short and steep, with easy ways up and down in many places, which helps with setting up laps.

co_dome_with_a_view.blurb: Dome With a View is a granite dome in the Red Feather Lakes region northwest of Fort Collins, near West Elkhorn Creek. The climbing is mostly trad with a few bolted sport lines, and the grades lean toward the harder end: a scattering of 5.6 to 5.9 routes, then a solid block of 5.10 and especially 5.11, topped by one 5.12. The dome has both a sunny side and a shady side over the course of a day, so you can choose a face to suit the weather. It suits confident leaders looking for granite cracks and faces in a pleasant lakes-and-domes setting.

co_north_quarry_pinnacle_area.blurb: North Quarry / Pinnacle Area sits at the western end of the main cliff band on North Table Mountain, just outside Golden. The rock is a dark lava porphyry, and the band faces south and west, which makes it a comfortable choice on cold days. Routes are generally short, around 60 feet. About half are trad, including crack and chimney lines near 5.8, and the rest are bolted, with a spread of 5.11 and 5.12 sport pitches and a couple of 5.13s on top. Warm weather can leave the holds polished and slick, and rattlesnakes are around in summer and fall.
